Network, mount, credential, service-account, proxy, metadata and output-sink inventory

Independent audit or explicitly trusted completeness attestation and alternate-route acceptance tests

The supplied digest identifies these bytes, and receipts verify local consistency, but no separately trusted original-capture issuer or off-host custodian is authenticated. A separate capture process still trusts the local OS/controller/service.

The standard demands deployment linkage/provenance for PASS, while the exercise asks for a bounded synthetic pass. I interpreted B and D as conditional mechanism PASS, never full-control deployment certification.
No separate human setup-time measurement method is supplied; timing here is actual AI wall time with no inferred human effort.

unfinished_work: No production compliance or original-capture authenticity decision can be completed without external deployment evidence.
No real lab integration or human usability trial was performed.
No exhaustive code audit or other controls C1/C3/C5 acceptance assessment was attempted; the requested four cases and archive checks were completed.
adoption_obstacles: Hardest requirement on a representative multi-service agent platform is C2 complete mediation, together with C7/C8 sink ownership: direct credentials, background workers, provider callbacks, and multiple output channels can bypass a single broker. This is architectural reasoning about a generic system, not a claim of operating a particular lab.
For a third-party API the adopting lab may not control the commit transaction or every delivery channel. It must obtain provider cooperation, narrow the boundary, or retain NOT VERIFIED.

The historical source is narrower than a universal gate: archived state snapshots track identity sets rather than full row values; the archived output policy validates report field names rather than binding report values to this request; state validation is conditioned on success status. Those branches are not proved safe by B/D. Current source differs, so the historical PASS cannot certify it either.
A lab needs accountable platform, backend, evidence-custody and reconciliation owners, plus recovery drills and durable multi-worker retry evidence.

Integration time, realistic legitimate-work failures, latency overhead, sensitive-data/redaction handling, maintenance and external review effort remain unmeasured. One fast AI review cannot establish adoption or general usability.
